sections.title: Scalability vs High Availability: Vertical, Horizontal and Multi-AZ
keyTopics: ASG scale out and scale in
sections.objective: Distinguish vertical scaling, horizontal scaling and high availability, and select the correct EC2 mechanism (instance resizing, Auto Scaling Group, multi-AZ deployment) for a given load or failure-tolerance requirement.

sections.title: Elastic Load Balancer Fundamentals: Purpose, Health Checks and Security Groups
keyTopics: Load balancer single DNS access point
Health checks on port and route
Application security group restricting to LB
sections.objective: Explain why a managed Elastic Load Balancer is used and how health checks and chained security groups keep traffic flowing only to healthy instances from the load balancer.

sections.title: Load Balancer Types: Classic, ALB, NLB and Gateway
keyTopics: ALB query string and header routing
ALB target groups (EC2, ECS, Lambda, IPs)
sections.objective: Choose the appropriate load balancer type (CLB, ALB, NLB, GWLB) for a scenario based on protocol, layer, performance, static IP and appliance-inspection requirements.

sections.title: Sticky Sessions, Cross-Zone Load Balancing and SSL/TLS Certificates
keyTopics: Cross-zone load balancing default per ELB
sections.objective: Apply stickiness, cross-zone load balancing and SNI-based multi-certificate HTTPS configurations, and identify which ELB types support each feature and where extra costs apply.

sections.title: Connection Draining and Auto Scaling Groups
keyTopics: ASG with load balancer health checks
sections.objective: Explain connection draining behaviour and configure Auto Scaling Group capacities, launch templates and load balancer registration to keep capacity matched to demand and replace unhealthy instances.

sections.title: Auto Scaling Policies, Metrics and Cooldowns
sections.objective: Select the right scaling policy and metric for a workload scenario, and explain how cooldown periods and AMI readiness affect how quickly an ASG stabilizes.

notes: Exam emphasis (Task 2.1, 2.2, 3.2): expect scenario questions comparing ALB (layer 7, path/host routing, Lambda targets) with NLB (layer 4, static IP, extreme performance) and GWLB (layer 3, GENEVE 6081); know cross-zone defaults (ALB on, NLB/GWLB off with inter-AZ charges), SNI limits (no CLB), and that CLB supports only one certificate. Common distractor traps: confusing scale up/out, treating ASG as a cost item (ASG itself is free), forgetting health checks need a 200 on a port+path, and assuming scheduled scaling reacts to load. Background note: Launch Configurations are deprecated; launch templates are the tested option.
